data.name: Telemetry
data.detailed_description:
In the early 22nd century, AI-driven productivity generated a global surplus that never reached the people who needed it. Instead, it funded a new class of extragovernmental agencies, among them the Department of Conjoint Space Efforts, tasked with advancing humanity's reach into the final frontier.

The world watched as the DCSE's most ambitious probe, the Pioneer, made its way to a now-classified destination. When it finally arrived, its signal inexplicably corrupted all AI systems on Earth.

Years later, the DCSE began replacing its artificial systems with human operators as part of a jobs initiative. This is where you come in.

The Terminal Interface

Monitor deep-space feeds, read classified bulletins, and communicate with your colleagues; all from the cold glow of a DCSE operator terminal. It is an outdated interface barely human-friendly, maybe reinstated in a rush after the Pioneer incident.

Probe Orientation & Camera Control

Point your cameras at distant moons, gas giants, and binary stars. Report what you find. The work is mundane, but you are among the first humans to ever lay eyes on these worlds.

Hands-on Diagnostics

Your on-probe systems can only do so much. Conduct spectral analyses, decode telemetry signals, and interpret data too complex for the satellite hardware. And when the feed goes dark, it is on you to bring it back.

A Deeper Narrative

Something is unsettling your colleagues, as your observations don't quite match the official reports. At the end of every session, something out there forcefully terminates your connection. You have to wonder: is this what happened to the Pioneer?

Features

  • 3 episodic chapters of atmospheric narrative horror.

  • Unique scientifically inspired puzzles across every episode: logic circuits, signal decoding, spectral analysis, and more.

  • A retro-futuristic terminal interface with a deep-space probe camera to navigate.

  • A slow-burn mystery told through official bulletins, a team chatroom, and cryptic transmissions.

data.short_description: An atmospheric cosmic horror story told through a retro-futuristic terminal. On your first day at a secretive transnational space agency, you'll operate deep-space probes, and explore a silent galaxy. Until you are noticed...

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • Requires a 64-bit processor and operating system
  • OS: Windows 10 64-bit
  • Processor: Any 64-bit dual-core processor from 2015 or later (e.g. Intel Core i3-6100, AMD FX-6300)
  • Memory: 4 GB RAM
  • Graphics: DirectX 11 capable GPU, 1 GB VRAM. Integrated graphics (e.g. Intel HD 520 or newer) are also sufficient.
  • DirectX: Version 11
  • Storage: 1 GB available space
  • Sound Card: Any
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recommended:
  • Requires a 64-bit processor and operating system
  • OS: Windows 10 or 11 64-bit
  • Processor: Any 64-bit quad-core processor from 2018 or later (e.g. Intel Core i5-8400, AMD Ryzen 5 2600)
  • Memory: 8 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 / AMD Radeon RX 560 or better
  • DirectX: Version 12
  • Storage: 1 GB available space
  • Sound Card: Any

mac_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS: macOS 13 Ventura
  • Processor: Apple M1, or any Intel Mac from 2015 or later
  • Memory: 4 GB RAM
  • Graphics: Any Metal-capable GPU. Integrated graphics are sufficient
  • Storage: 1 GB available space
  • Sound Card: Any
mac_requirements.recommended:
Recommended:
  • OS: macOS 15 Sequoia or newer
  • Processor: Apple M1 or newer
  • Memory: 8 GB RAM
  • Graphics: Apple Silicon integrated GPU or dedicated AMD GPU
  • Storage: 1 GB available space
  • Sound Card: Any
